### Observed differences

- In the later window, activity A06 appears in about 30 in 100 traces, up from about 7 in 100, and its mean position shifts from about two‑thirds of the trace length to about one‑quarter, i.e. it occurs earlier. [OCC001, POS001]
- A06’s outgoing behaviour changes: before it led to a spread of ten activities, after it leads to A16 in about 85 in 100 of its occurrences. A15, which previously went to A16 in about 97 in 100 cases, now goes to A16 in about 85 and to A06 in about 15. [DIR001, DIR002]
- Several activities that previously led mainly to A33 or A29 now lead mainly to A27: A19 (from 54% A33/44% A29 to 98% A27), A20 (from 55% A33/45% A29 to 96% A27), A25 (from 53% A33/43% A29 to 95% A27), A26 (from 41% A33/59% A29 to 92% A27). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- A28’s successors concentrate on A29 (about 98 in 100, up from about 50), and A29’s successors concentrate on A33 (about 99 in 100, up from about 48). [DIR007, DIR008]
- A46, which before went to A27 in about 95 in 100 cases, now goes to A25, A26, A19 and A20 (about 29, 23, 22 and 22 in 100 respectively) and only about 1.5 in 100 to A27. [DIR009]
- A06 now co‑occurs with A16, A27, A28, A29, A33 and A46 in about 30 in 100 traces (up from about 6.5), and in most of those it occurs before them (e.g. A06 before A27 in about 27.5 in 100 traces, up from about 1.5). [REL001, REL002, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- The order of A19, A20, A25 and A26 relative to A27 and A28 flips: before, A27/A28 came before these activities in about 22–27 in 100 traces; after, these activities come before A27/A28 in about 22–31 in 100 traces. [REL010–REL017]
- A19, A20, A25 and A26 all shift earlier in the trace (mean position from about 0.59–0.61 to about 0.33), while A27, A28 and A29 shift slightly later (mean increases of about 0.03–0.04). [POS002–POS008]
- Lag distributions change accordingly, e.g. A06–A16 becomes mostly a lag‑1 pair (94% vs 0% before), A06–A27 becomes mostly lag‑5 (97% vs 50% before), and A15–A27 becomes mostly lag‑5 (98% vs 12% before). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which a new activity, A06, is inserted early in the process, and a re‑routing occurs: many activities (A19, A20, A25, A26) that previously led to A33 or A29 now lead to A27, while A46 no longer leads to A27 but instead to A25, A26, A19 and A20. The order of A19/A20/A25/A26 relative to A27/A28 also flips, consistent with these activities moving earlier. The number of qualifying evidence items (53) is far above the 0.78 expected by chance, and the pattern is consistent across occurrence, direction, position, relation and lag indicators. A competing explanation is that the two windows simply contain different mixes of process variants; however, the breadth and consistency of the differences make a genuine structural change the more plausible interpretation. Some lag items involving A06 rest on very few before‑window observations (1–2 traces), so those specific lag estimates are weak, but they are not needed for the main conclusion.
